about: Stages and timing for the catalog-truth playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: parity
stages.do: Compare the Discovery and Engagement catalogs on a sample: missing products, stock, price, sale price, URL, image and title. Add each failing check as a finding.

stages.name: prices
stages.do: Find wrong prices across the whole Discovery catalog, each with its owner. Add each failing check as a finding for the feed or pricing team.

stages.name: variants
stages.do: Check the products on page one and the top sellers at variant level: stock, prices, SKUs and images. Add each failing check as a finding for the feed team.

stages.name: fix
stages.do: Fix the Engagement catalog items the parity check found wrong, each batch after its own yes. Record not_needed when the parity check found nothing to fix there.

skip_when.reason: all three checks were clean: there is nothing to fix.

stages.name: recheck
stages.do: Run the parity check again on the same catalogs: did the fixes hold through the next import, and did the feed team's fixes land?

skip_when.reason: all three checks were clean: there is nothing to recheck.

the catalogs were in sync and nothing was fixed in Engagement, so a second parity check has nothing to compare. Re-run price-anomaly-finder or discovery-variant-health for the Discovery-side findings instead.

notes.recheck_after_days: Days after the fix stage finishes before the recheck stage is due. engagement-catalog-fixer's fixes last only until the next catalog import overwrites them, and the feed team needs time to fix the Discovery side; a week covers several import cycles and a working week.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. requires_both: true means the playbook compares Discovery and Engagement, so new refuses a run without --account, --environment and --project-id. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, which product it needs in a run on both (product), what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done) and skip_when (suggest skipping when an earlier stage had one of these outcomes, or with skipped: true when it was skipped; an entry with all lists conditions that must every one hold). The fix stage records not_needed rather than being skipped when there's nothing to fix in Engagement but the other checks found problems: its date starts the recheck wait, which the feed team's fixes need too. When all three checks were clean, status suggests skipping both the fix and the recheck.
